issues.body: The removed host step ran `rustup component add clippy rustfmt` from the target working directory, after rustup had selected/materialized any `rust-toolchain.toml` override. This Dockerfile instead adds the components while building an empty-context image, so it adds them only to the image's default 1.88.0 toolchain. At runtime, a target that pins another channel causes rustup to install/select that toolchain, but `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` are then unavailable unless the target happened to list those components itself. All three cargo profiles invoke fmt and/or clippy, so a legitimate pinned workspace can now fail for missing components. The new tests validate the docker argv and wrapper call sites but never exercise a non-default pinned toolchain, despite the comments explicitly claiming that pin materialization is preserved.
issues.fix_hint: Provision `rustfmt` and `clippy` for the active target-selected toolchain inside the sandbox after mounting `/workspace` and before running gate commands (still with no host fallback), or otherwise make the image support the selected override. Add a non-vacuous test using a toolchain different from the image default that proves both `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` are available.
issues.title: Pinned target toolchains do not receive clippy and rustfmt

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The containment direction is sound, but the replacement does not preserve the existing Rust-toolchain semantics for repositories that pin a toolchain. The image installs clippy/rustfmt only for its default 1.88 toolchain; a target pin is resolved later at container runtime, where those components are not provisioned. This can make valid pinned workspaces fail before their policy gate runs. The self-tests exercise only argv/source structure and therefore do not catch this advertised behavior.
